This chapter teaches the words for pointing at things: **this / that** — ده (da), دي (di) and دول (dol) — and how to name the objects around you. Tap any sentence to reveal its franco and English.

## How it works

**One set covers both "this" and "that".** Egyptian doesn't split them: **ده (da)** for a masculine thing, **دي (di)** for a feminine thing, **دول (dol)** for plural — used for near *and* far alike. A gesture or the word **هناك (henak)** "there" marks distance when you need it.

**Two structures, and the contrast matters:**

- **After a noun** (the noun takes ال): **الكتاب ده (el-ketab da)** = "this book". Here the demonstrative is just describing.
- **At the front, as the subject:** **ده كتاب (da ketab)** = "this **is** a book". Egyptian has no verb "to be", so the bare demonstrative + noun already means "this is…".

So *el-ketab da* (this book) and *da ketab* (this is a book) are different sentences — watch the word order.

**Asking:** **ده إيه؟ (da eh?)** / **دي إيه؟ (di eh?)** = "what's this?".

**Whose is it — بتاع (betaa3).** To say "mine / yours", use بتاع, which agrees with the thing owned and then takes an ending: **الكتاب ده بتاعي (el-ketab da bta3i)** "this book is mine"; for a feminine thing, بتاعتي (bta3ti).

## Demonstratives

| Arabic - franco | English             |
|-----------------|---------------------|
| ده - da         | this / that (m.)    |
| دي - di         | this / that (f.)    |
| دول - dol       | these / those (pl.) |
| هنا - hena      | here                |
| هناك - henak    | there               |

## The two structures

<details class="frase">

<summary>الكتاب ده</summary>

[el-ketab da]{.fr} [this book (noun + demonstrative)]{.en}

</details>

<details class="frase">

<summary>ده كتاب</summary>

[da ketab]{.fr} [this is a book (demonstrative as subject)]{.en}

</details>

<details class="frase">

<summary>دي شنطة</summary>

[di shanta]{.fr} [this is a bag]{.en}

</details>

<details class="frase">

<summary>دول كتب</summary>

[dol kutob]{.fr} [these are books]{.en}

</details>

## Using demonstratives in a sentence

For "I want / I see / it's mine" you can use a couple of words that just agree
in gender (the full verbs come in their own chapters). Negate them with
**مش (mesh)**.

| English | Masculine | franco | Feminine | franco |
|---------|-----------|--------|----------|--------|
| wanting | عايز      | 3ayez  | عايزة    | 3ayza  |
| seeing  | شايف      | shayef | شايفة    | shayfa |

**Negative forms with مش:**

| English     | Masculine | franco     | Feminine  | franco     |
|-------------|-----------|------------|-----------|------------|
| not wanting | مش عايز   | mesh 3ayez | مش عايزة  | mesh 3ayza |
| not seeing  | مش شايف   | mesh shayef| مش شايفة  | mesh shayfa|

**Examples:**

<details class="frase">
<summary>أنا مش عايز عربية، أنا عايز عجلة.</summary>
<span class="fr">ana mesh 3ayez 3arabiyya, ana 3ayez 3agala.</span>
<span class="en">I don't want a car, I want a bicycle. (m.)</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>هي عايزة فستان، مش عايزة قميص.</summary>
<span class="fr">heyya 3ayza fustan, mesh 3ayza 2amis.</span>
<span class="en">She wants a dress, not a shirt.</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>أنا مش شايف الموبايل.</summary>
<span class="fr">ana mesh shayef el-mobail.</span>
<span class="en">I don't see the phone. (m.)</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">
<summary>إنتي شايفة القطة؟ لا، أنا مش شايفة القطة.</summary>
<span class="fr">enti shayfa el-2otta? la2, ana mesh shayfa el-2otta.</span>
<span class="en">Do you see the cat? No, I don't see the cat. (f.)</span>
</details>

<details class="frase">

<summary>عايز الكرسي ده</summary>

[3ayez el-korsi da]{.fr} [I want this chair]{.en}

</details>

<details class="frase">

<summary>شايف الحصان هناك</summary>

[shayef el-7osan henak]{.fr} [I see that horse (over there)]{.en}

</details>

<details class="frase">

<summary>الشنطة دي بتاعتي</summary>

[el-shanta di bta3ti]{.fr} [this bag is mine]{.en}

</details>

<details class="frase">

<summary>مش عايز القميص ده</summary>

[mesh 3ayez el-2amis da]{.fr} [I don't want this shirt]{.en}

</details>

## Dialogue: "What's this?"

Sherif is looking around Nadia's place.

[شريف — Sherif]{.rotulo}

<details class="frase">

<summary>ده إيه؟</summary>

[da eh?]{.fr} [What's this?]{.en}

</details>

[نادية — Nadia]{.rotulo}

<details class="frase">

<summary>ده موبايل</summary>

[da mobile]{.fr} [It's a phone]{.en}

</details>

[شريف — Sherif]{.rotulo}

<details class="frase">

<summary>الموبايل ده بتاعك؟</summary>

[el-mobile da bta3ek?]{.fr} [Is this phone yours?]{.en}

</details>

[نادية — Nadia]{.rotulo}

<details class="frase">

<summary>لأ، ده مش بتاعي. ده بتاع أختي</summary>

[la2, da mesh bta3i. da bta3 o5ti]{.fr} [No, it's not mine. It's my sister's]{.en}

</details>

[شريف — Sherif]{.rotulo}

<details class="frase">

<summary>والقطة دي؟</summary>

[wel-2otta di?]{.fr} [And this cat?]{.en}

</details>

[نادية — Nadia]{.rotulo}

<details class="frase">

<summary>أيوة، دي بتاعتي</summary>

[aywa, di bta3ti]{.fr} [Yes, she's mine]{.en}

</details>

## Exercises

Try each one out loud first, then tap **Show answer**.

### Exercise 1 — ده، دي or دول؟

Choose the demonstrative that agrees with the noun.

**1.** الكتاب \_\_\_ *(book, m.)*

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[ده]{.ar} [el-ketab da]{.fr}

</details>

**2.** الترابيزة \_\_\_ *(table, f.)*

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[دي]{.ar} [el-tarabeza di]{.fr}

</details>

**3.** الكلاب \_\_\_ *(dogs, pl.)*

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[دول]{.ar} [el-kilab dol]{.fr}

</details>

**4.** القطة \_\_\_ *(cat, f.)*

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[دي]{.ar} [el-2otta di]{.fr}

</details>

**5.** الكرسي \_\_\_ *(chair, m.)*

<details class="ans">

<summary>Show answer</summary>

[ده]{.ar} [el-korsi da]{.fr}

</details>
